faq.label: Questions
faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How often should I have a check-up?
faq.a1: For healthy teeth, we recommend a check-up and a cleaning every six months. That way problems are caught before they grow. Some conditions call for more frequent visits.
faq.q2: What are the benefits of a professional cleaning?
faq.a2: It removes plaque and tartar, helps prevent gum disease, freshens your breath and brightens your smile. And your dentist can spot problems early.
faq.a3: Yes. Our whitening is safe and carried out by professionals, for your comfort and the best result.
faq.q4: Is whitening at the dentist better than a home kit?
faq.a4: It’s usually more effective and safer: the dentist uses a stronger agent and protects your gums, so the results are faster and more visible.
faq.q5: What should I do in an emergency?
faq.a5: Severe pain, a knocked-out tooth or a broken filling: call the clinic straight away.
faq.q6: How long does a whitening session take?
faq.a6: 30 to 60 minutes in the chair. Depending on what you’d like and your natural shade, more sessions are sometimes needed.

tm.2.q: I was nervous about visiting the dentist after years of avoiding treatment, but the professionals at Elite Smile were incredibly patient and caring. The clinic is modern, clean, and welcoming, and the results exceeded my expectations.
tm.3.q: Excellent service, friendly staff, and amazing attention to detail. The dentists truly care about their patients and take the time to explain every step. I’ve received so many compliments on my new smile — highly recommended!

dp.label: Dentist at Elite Smile
dp.clinics: Elite Smile welcomes you in Eindhoven and Hoogland.
t.controle.w: The dentist checks your whole mouth: teeth, gums, jaw and the soft tissues, and talks you through what they see.
t.reiniging.w: Tartar and plaque are removed above and below the gumline. Good against gum inflammation and for fresh breath.
t.polijsten.w: After the cleaning, your teeth are polished smooth, so stains are less likely to build up.
t.rontgen.w: Small X-rays show cavities between the teeth and the bone; a panoramic X-ray shows all your teeth and your jaw.
t.vulling.w: The decayed part is removed and the tooth is restored with a white filling in the colour of your tooth.
t.kind-controle.w: A calm check-up at your child’s pace, with explanations for you and a sticker for your child.
t.kind-vulling.w: A cavity in a baby tooth or a permanent tooth is cleaned and filled, calmly and with clear explanations.
t.pulpa-kind.w: If the nerve of a baby tooth is inflamed, the diseased part is removed, so the tooth can stay until it falls out naturally.
t.fluoride.w: A layer of fluoride strengthens the enamel and helps prevent cavities.
t.ruimtebehouder.s: Keeping room for the permanent tooth
t.ruimtebehouder.w: If a baby tooth is lost too early, a small appliance keeps the space open for the permanent tooth.
t.facings.s: Thin shells for a new front
t.facings.w: Thin shells of porcelain or composite are placed on the front of your teeth: a different colour, shape or position.
t.hollywood.w: Veneers on all visible teeth, often combined with whitening and gum contouring, based on a smile design.
t.gingiva.w: Excess or uneven gum tissue is reshaped, so your teeth look in proportion and your smile looks more balanced.
t.diastema.w: A gap between your teeth is closed, usually with tooth-coloured composite, without grinding the teeth down.
t.bleken.w: A whitening agent lightens your natural teeth; the dentist protects your gums. Sometimes more sessions are needed.
t.beugel.w: Brackets on your teeth and a wire straighten your teeth step by step over a few years.
t.uitneembaar.s: A plate you put in and take out yourself
t.uitneembaar.w: A removable appliance guides the growth of the jaw or moves teeth, mainly in children.
t.retainer.w: A fixed wire behind your teeth or a removable retainer holds the result of your braces in place.
t.extractie.w: A tooth that can no longer be saved is removed under local anaesthetic.
t.verstandskies.w: A wisdom tooth that has fully erupted is removed without opening the gum.
t.bot.w: Where there is too little jawbone, bone or a bone substitute is placed, so an implant can be fitted later.
t.wortelkanaal.w: The inflamed or dead nerve is removed, and the canals are cleaned and sealed. That way you keep your own tooth.
t.herbehandeling.w: If a previously treated tooth becomes inflamed again, the old root filling is removed and the canal is cleaned once more.
t.kroon.w: A crown fully covers a weak or damaged tooth and restores its shape and strength.
t.brug.w: A bridge fills the space of a missing tooth with a new tooth attached to the neighbouring teeth.
t.prothese.w: A removable denture replaces a few or all of your teeth, custom-made over a few appointments.
t.implantaat.w: A titanium screw in the jaw takes the place of the root. Once it has fused with the bone, a crown is placed on top.
v.7: As advised, often twice a year
v.16: Three or four appointments over 3 to 6 months
c.controle.h1: What the dentist saw will be in the app afterwards.
c.controle.h2: A check-up and a cleaning every six months.
c.reiniging.h1: A little bleeding of the gums or sensitivity to cold settles within a few days.
c.reiniging.h2: Keep using interdental brushes or floss every day.
c.rontgen.h1: Pregnant, or might you be? Tell us beforehand.
c.rontgen.h2: The dentist will go through the X-rays with you.
c.vulling.h1: Don’t eat while you’re still numb.
c.vulling.h2: A white filling is hard straight away.
c.kind-vulling.h1: Make sure your child doesn’t bite their numb lip.
c.kind-vulling.h2: Eating is fine again once the feeling comes back.
c.pulpa-kind.h1: Soft food today, and no biting on the tooth.
c.pulpa-kind.h2: Swelling or fever? Call the clinic.
c.fluoride.h1: Don’t eat or drink for the first half hour.
c.fluoride.h2: Wait until the next morning to brush again.
c.ruimtebehouder.h1: No toffees, chewing gum or liquorice.
c.ruimtebehouder.h2: Brush carefully around it every evening.
c.facings.r: Straight away, with a few days of sensitivity.
c.facings.h1: Don’t bite your nails, pens or ice.
c.facings.h2: After two weeks, the dentist checks that everything fits well.
c.gingiva.h1: Soft, lukewarm food for two days.
c.bonding.h1: The composite is hard straight away; you can eat normally.
c.bonding.h2: Rinse with water after coffee or tea.
c.beugel.r: A few days to get used to it.
c.beugel.h1: Brush after every meal, including between wire and tooth.
c.beugel.h2: A bracket rubbing? A small ball of wax helps.
c.uitneembaar.r: A few days to get used to it.
c.uitneembaar.h1: Wear it for as many hours as your dentist says.
c.uitneembaar.h2: Clean it with cold or lukewarm water, never hot.
c.retainer.h2: A fixed wire? Clean under it every day with an interdental brush.
c.extractie.r: Usually back at work the next day; the wound closes in 1 to 2 weeks.
c.extractie.h1: Bite firmly on the gauze for 30 minutes.
c.extractie.h2: No rinsing for 24 hours, no smoking for 72 hours.
c.implantaat.r: The wound closes in 1 to 2 weeks; the implant fuses with the bone in 3 to 6 months.
c.implantaat.h1: Cool your cheek and don’t touch the area.
c.implantaat.h2: No strenuous exercise for the first 48 hours.
c.bot.r: The wound closes in 2 weeks; the bone needs a few months.
c.bot.h1: A few small granules in your mouth are normal.
c.bot.h2: In the upper jaw? Don’t blow your nose hard for a week.
c.wortelkanaal.r: Tender for a few days; then a filling or crown.
c.wortelkanaal.h1: Don’t chew hard on the treated tooth.
c.wortelkanaal.h2: A crown often follows: plan it in good time.
c.kroon.h1: With a temporary crown: no chewing gum or toffees.
c.kroon.h2: Floss, then pull the floss out sideways, not upwards.
c.prothese.r: A few weeks to get used to it.
c.prothese.h1: Start with soft food in small pieces.
c.prothese.h2: A sore spot? Call us and we’ll adjust it.
c.bleken.r: Straight away, with one or two days of sensitivity.
c.bleken.h1: A white diet for 48 hours: no coffee, tea or red wine.
